disclaimer: Corrected candidate semantics for M_MVP v2. Every number is a tagged public data/manual value, an explicit scenario choice, or a named candidate value. [V]=0 and no build is pinned, so nothing here is a Civ6 fact and no number is a real-game optimum. Certified claims are limited to OptimalAt(theta, sigma, N(theta)) for the argmin and argmax theta; all other N and the envelope are untrusted search estimates.

corrections.was: v1 credited settler progress on every step, including IDLE steps and steps taken at pop 1 (free production banking across the PrereqPopulation=2 boundary)
corrections.now: R-SET-9: prog += q only when build = SETTLER; SETTLER is legal only when the PRE-TURN pop >= 2; IDLE and all pop-1 steps leave prog unchanged
corrections.effect: v1 predictions 15/16/20 and the v1 witness are INVALID; recomputed N is 20 (cost 80) / 25 (cost 110)

corrections.was: build legality ambiguous w.r.t. same-step growth
corrections.now: selection timing fixed: build is chosen against the pre-turn state; a growth event never retro-legalises SETTLER (assumption A8)
corrections.effect: gates the growth step: no settler progress on the step where pop 1 -> 2

corrections.now: extra must be a real unworked tile of sigma, is canonicalised to none when build = IDLE, and contributes production only if a growth event actually occurs; otherwise it yields nothing (no ghost output)
corrections.effect: no observable change on optimal lines; removes a modelling loophole

corrections.was: G1 claimed threshold rounding never bites
corrections.now: T(3) IS evaluated because pop 3 is reachable (earliest ~t=18), so thresholdRounding is a new axis C7 {3300 floor, 3383 exact}; what is claimed (and must be proved + enumerated) is only the pop-4 ceiling: from pop 3 the max surplus is 110/step so T(3)>=3300 needs >=30 more steps, i.e. pop 4 at t>=48 > H

corrections.was: G6 justified the 1/100 grid by 'denominators divide 100'
corrections.now: G6 justified by the actual finite per-step yield set: multipliers are applied once per step to that step's yield (d in {0,100,200} -> e in {0,110,220}; P in {300..800} -> P*21/20 in {315..840}), never to accumulated state, and accumulation is integer addition

certified claims are only the argmin/argmax theta; per-theta N for the other 126 and the envelope [20,25] are labelled search estimates until all 128 are certified or an inertness lemma for C2-C7 is proved

rules.statement: a settler can only be built when pop >= 2, judged at build selection time
completion costs 1 population
no technology prerequisite
the city keeps growing while a settler is under construction

settler progress is credited only on a step whose build = SETTLER; SETTLER is selectable only when the pre-turn pop >= 2, so nothing is banked across the prerequisite and IDLE steps credit nothing
rules.source: derived from R-SET-4 (settler not selectable below pop 2) + R-PROD-2/3 (progress is per item, overflow goes to the *next* item built)
rules.note: v2 correction FIX-1/FIX-2; selection timing itself is assumption A8. v2.1: the production-side helper is total (extraGain(none) = 0) so the step function is defined on every legal action, including the witness growth step (IDLE + newCitizen=best).

stepPseudocode: legal(s,a): |a.work| <= s.pop; a.extra = none or a.extra in tiles - a.work; a.build = SETTLER => s.pop(preturn) >= 2; a.build = IDLE => a.extra = none; post-modifier surplus >= 0 (legal iff step returns some)
F = 200 + sum(food(t) for t in a.work)                     # a.extra NEVER contributes food

P = 300 + sum(prod(t) for t in a.work)                     # 300 = city centre 100 + palace 200
extraGain(e) = 0 if e = none else prod(e)                  # TOTAL in both branches (v2.1 / B1)
grow(b,p) = if b >= T(p) then (p+1, basket(b-T(p))) else (p,b)
CREDIT(q) = q if a.build = SETTLER else 0                  # R-SET-9
GROWTH_FIRST: d = F - 200*pop; require d >= 0; e = d*growthMult(tier(pop))/100
if pop1 > pop and theta.newCitizen = best then P += extraGain(a.extra)   # 0 when none/IDLE
if a.build = SETTLER and prog1 >= cost then (pop1-1, food1, prog1-cost, trained+1) else (pop1, food1, prog1, trained)
PRODUCTION_FIRST: q = round10(P*prodMult(tier(pop))/100); prog1 = prog + CREDIT(q)
done = (a.build = SETTLER and prog1 >= cost); pop1 = pop - done; prog1 = prog1 - cost*done
d = F - 200*pop1; require d >= 0; e = d*growthMult(tier(pop1))/100
(pop2,food2) = grow(food+e, pop1); return (pop2, food2, prog1, trained+done)
tier(p) from amenityStock - req(p); growthMult 110/100/85, prodMult 105/100/95 (per cent of the 1/100 value)

guards.name: threshold scope and population ceiling (labels corrected in v2.1)
guards.detail: The model DEFINES T(3) and T(4); the claim is that neither is ever reached. Earliest pop 2 is t=7 (ceil(1500/220)); earliest pop 3 is t >= 7 + ceil(2400/220) = 18; at pop 3 the max surplus is 100 (F <= 700, consumption 600) so e <= 110/step. Hence at any t <= H=34 food at pop 3 is <= 110*(34-18)+219 = 1979 < 3300: T(3) is never crossed, so C7 is inert BY PROOF (not 'active'), and pop 4 (t >= 48) is unreachable. The invariant food < T(pop) holds in every stored state by construction.
guards.measured: analyst measurement, NOT certified: max pop 3; max pop-3 food 100 (zero) / 170 (subtract) at cost 80 and 600/670 at cost 110; O8 must re-derive

observed.note: analyst measurement over the 128-combo run, NOT certified; O8 must re-derive. Pop-3 food is bounded analytically by 110*(H-18)+219 = 1979 < 3300, so no stored pop-3 food figure is claimed here.

guards.name: housing inert
guards.detail: housing 6: pop<=3 => left>=3>=2 => factor 1.00; even pop 4 gives left=2 => 1.00. Breaks only above pop 4 or on a non-fresh-water capital.

guards.name: one growth per settlement
guards.detail: max surplus 220 < T(1)=1500, so two threshold crossings in one step are impossible.

guards.name: population ceiling pop<=3
guards.detail: same arithmetic as G1; the implementation must confirm the observed max pop over all reachable non-goal states for t<=H.

guards.name: idle civilians are a safe relaxation
guards.detail: |work| < pop enlarges the action set, so a lower bound proved with it still holds; with R-SET-9 IDLE only forfeits progress, so the achievability witness must be idle-free.

guards.name: scale sufficiency (premises added in v2.1)
guards.detail: Multipliers act exactly once per step on that step's yield, never on accumulated state. Given G2 and tier in {Happy, Content} for amenityStock in {1,2} (so req(p) <= 1 for p <= 3): surplus d in {0,100,200} -> e in {0,110,220}; production P in {300..700} (sum of tile production <= 400) -> P*21/20 in {315..735}; all integers in 1/100, closed under integer addition. A Displeased tier combined with a 0.50 housing factor (e = 42.5) would break the grid; G2/G3 and amenityStock in {1,2} exclude it.

fixedNonCandidateSettings.note: Post-modifier surplus < 0 is not an action. Restriction class: it removes actions, so it can only raise N and cannot carry a real-game lower bound; inert here only because at pop 1-3 the max-production assignment is food-neutral or better (PH d=100, PH+P d=0, GH+PH+P d=0) and pop 4 has no legal action. Inertness is obligation O8, not an assumption.
R-SET-9 / FIX-1: no credit at pop 1 and none on IDLE steps. The no-carry-across-idle-step rule is a second RESTRICTION (it can only raise N); a <= q carry would move N to 19/24 (outside the box).
